s1.where: the greeting page with the writing box at the bottom
s1.expectation: The start page where I'd begin a new chat, I think. The main 'home' spot.
s1.cue: The big 'Back at it, Ally Cooper' in the middle and the 'Chat with Claude...' box at the bottom.

first_pass.why: The biggest words on the page are a hello to me, not a name for the place. Nothing at the top says 'New chat' or 'Home'. I work it out from the writing box, but that's me doing detective work, and there's an upgrade strip right in my eyeline too.
first_pass.solution: Put a short plain name at the top, like 'New chat', and keep the greeting smaller underneath it.

test_cases.task: The app opens on the page with the large greeting in the middle and the writing box at the bottom (if it is not already there: open the menu with the three lines at the top left and tap the big word at the top of the menu). Put the phone down, look away and count slowly to ten, then look back at the screen and, before touching anything, say where you are. Then drag the page up and down and watch whether a name for this page shows up anywhere. (The picture with the microphone warning cannot be brought back without the phone's permission prompts, so answer for that picture from this same page.)
test_cases.real_if: you still have to work out where you are from the writing box, and no name for the page appears anywhere
test_cases.not_real_if: you know straight away where you are, or a name for the page shows up
test_cases.persona_report: When I looked back, the middle said 'Coffee and Claude time?'. Nothing at the top names the page, only the three-line button and the ghost. Dragging up and down did nothing: the page doesn't move and no name appears. I only knew where I was from the 'Chat with Claude...' box at the bottom. The next time I came back, the greeting had changed to 'Good afternoon, Ally Cooper'. So the one big line of text isn't even the same from one visit to the next.
test_cases.what_they_did: The app was already on the greeting page. I looked away, came back and said where I was before touching anything. Then I dragged the page up and down. Later I came back to this page twice through the menu (tapping 'Claude' at the top).

s1.closing_comment: It's real, and worse than I thought: the page never names itself, and the big greeting changes every time, so I can't even use it as a landmark.

s2.where: the slide-out menu with Chats, Projects, Code, Artifacts
s2.expectation: The main menu that slides out from the side.
s2.cue: 'Claude' at the top and the list Chats / Projects / Code / Artifacts with the New chat button.

first_pass.why: I can tell it's a menu, but none of the four items is lit up, so I can't tell where I came from or which section I'm 'in'. 'Claude' is just the app's name, it doesn't tell me anything.
first_pass.solution: Highlight the item for the page I was on, clearly, and maybe call the top 'Menu' instead of just the app name.

test_cases.task: From the page with the greeting, tap the three lines at the top left to open the menu. Say which row, if any, shows the part of the app you came from. Then tap Chats, wait for it to open, open the menu again the same way, and compare.
test_cases.real_if: when opened from the greeting page, no row shows where you came from
test_cases.not_real_if: a row clearly shows where you came from
test_cases.persona_report: Opened from the greeting page, none of Chats, Projects, Code or Artifacts is marked. There are plain rows plus a 'Recents' list with two 'Untitled' items, so nothing says 'you came from here'. Opened from Chats, the Chats row has a soft grey pill behind it. It's there, but it's faint. So the menu only tells me where I am when I'm in one of those four sections, and not for the greeting page.
test_cases.what_they_did: From the greeting page I tapped the three lines, looked at which row was marked, then tapped Chats. On Chats I opened the menu again and compared.

s2.closing_comment: From the greeting page no row lights up. It only works after I've been in Chats or Code, and even then the pill is faint.

s3.expectation: An incognito (private) chat, a fresh one.
s3.cue: 'Incognito chat' at the top and the ghost with the sentence about staying out of history.

first_pass.why: The name is at the top and the ghost picture backs it up. The title is pale grey and small, but the picture and sentence in the middle confirm it fast.

s4.expectation: The upgrade page where I choose a paid plan.
s4.cue: Big 'Get more Claude' and 'Choose the plan right for you', and the Pro prices.

first_pass.why: Big bold heading, one clear job. I know exactly what this is (a sales page) straight away.

s5.where: the 'Add to chat' sheet with Camera, Photos, Files
s5.expectation: A little panel for adding things to my chat, popped up over the start page.
s5.cue: 'Add to chat' at the top of the panel, and the Camera / Photos / Files tiles.

first_pass.why: The panel has its own clear title and the X to close it. I know I'm still on the chat page underneath.

s6.cue: 'Select model' at the top of the panel and the tick next to Haiku 4.5.

first_pass.why: Clear title, and the tick shows what's chosen. Easy.

s7.expectation: A setup page for talking to Claude with my voice.
s7.cue: The microphone drawing and the big 'Send messages to Claude using your voice.'

first_pass.why: It's a sentence, not a name, but it's big and bold and the mic picture says it all. Three short points with icons — that's exactly how I like info.

s8.expectation: My list of past chats (empty right now).
s8.cue: 'Chats' at the top, the chat-bubbles picture and 'Your chats with Claude will show up here.'

first_pass.why: Short name at the top, one icon, one line. Perfect.

s9.expectation: The side menu, opened while I was on Chats.
s9.cue: The soft grey shading behind 'Chats' in the list.

first_pass.why: There's a shaded pill on Chats, so I can see which section I'm in. It's pretty faint though — I had to look twice.

s10.expectation: The Chats list, with a filter menu open.
s10.cue: 'Chats' at the top and the little menu with 'All' ticked.

first_pass.why: Title's still there, the drop-down is small and I can see what's ticked.

s11.expectation: A panel to put my chat into a project, but I don't have any projects.
s11.cue: 'Add to project' at the top of the panel, the back arrow, and the empty-box picture.

first_pass.why: Clear title and a back arrow so I know I can step back to the last panel.

s12.where: the 'Add to chat' sheet pulled up tall
s12.expectation: The same 'add to chat' panel, pulled right up, web search now on.

first_pass.why: Same clear title as before. Lots of white space, easy to scan.

s13.expectation: A panel telling me the model I picked needs a paid plan.
s13.cue: 'Upgrade to use Pro' and 'This model requires a Pro plan.'

first_pass.why: One title, one sentence, one button. I get it in two seconds.

s14.where: the microphone page with the language list open
s14.expectation: The voice setup page, with a list of languages open to choose from.
s14.cue: The microphone drawing at the top and the 'Speech Input Language' box peeking out underneath the list.

first_pass.why: The list is sitting right on top of the page's heading, so the words that told me what this page is have gone. I'm going off the mic drawing and the little grey label at the bottom.
first_pass.solution: Keep the heading visible when the list opens, or put a title on the list itself, like 'Choose your speaking language'.

test_cases.task: From the page with the greeting, tap the small microphone picture in the writing box (the grey one, not the round black button at the far right). On the page that opens, tap the box headed 'Speech Input Language' so its list drops down. Without choosing anything, say where you are. Then press the phone's Back button once to close the list, and compare. Do not press Continue. Leave with the X at the top left.
test_cases.real_if: while the list is open nothing tells you what page this is
test_cases.not_real_if: you can still tell what page this is while the list is open
test_cases.persona_report: With the list open, the big heading was covered, same as in the picture. But I'd tapped the box myself a second earlier, so I knew what the list was. The microphone drawing above it and the 'Speech Input Language' label under it both stayed in view. One Back press closed the list and the heading was right there again. The X took me straight back to the greeting page. Nothing asked for microphone permission.
test_cases.what_they_did: From the greeting page I tapped the small grey microphone in the writing box. The 'Send messages to Claude using your voice' page opened. I tapped the 'Speech Input Language' box and the list dropped down. I didn't choose anything. I pressed Back once to close the list, then left with the X. I did not press Continue.

s14.closing_comment: On the real phone I'd just opened that list myself, the mic drawing and label stayed in view, and one Back brought the heading back. A small wobble, not being lost.

s15.where: the microphone page with English (India) picked
s15.expectation: The voice setup page again, after picking a language.
s15.cue: 'Send messages to Claude using your voice.' and the language box showing English (India).

first_pass.why: Heading's back, the choice I made is showing. Fine.

first_pass.solution: A plain name at the top like 'New chat', and one thing at a time at the bottom — the warning could replace the upgrade strip instead of piling on top.

test_cases.task: Open the menu (three lines, top left) and tap Code. When it opens, look only at the top third of the screen for a few seconds and say where you are. Then read the rest of the page. Then open the menu again and see which row is marked. Do not press Upgrade; leave by opening the menu and tapping Chats.
test_cases.real_if: the top of the page does not tell you where you are and you have to read down to the middle
test_cases.not_real_if: you can tell where you are from the top of the page

When I opened the menu, the Code row had the faint grey pill, so the menu does back it up, but only if I think to open it.
test_cases.what_they_did: I opened the menu and tapped Code. I looked only at the top third for a few seconds, then read the rest. I took a second look to check whether anything was moving, opened the menu again, and left by tapping Chats. I did not press Upgrade.

s20.closing_comment: The top of the Code page still reads as someone's chat, and the real name is halfway down. The shaded Code row in the menu helps, but only if I go looking.
